question: True or false: modern black-and-white camera film can be developed under the red safelight used for printing?
answer: False. Black-and-white printing paper is made sensitive mainly to blue and green, so dim red or amber light cannot fog it. Most black-and-white film since the mid-twentieth century is panchromatic, sensitive to red as well, and must go into its developing tank in total darkness. The red-lit room of films is the printing stage.
move: Before copying a routine, check it was built for your material.
ask: Which routine of mine did I copy from someone without checking it was built for my situation?
trap: Picturing the red darkroom glow of films as the whole process.
reference: Michael Langford, Anna Fox & Richard Sawdon Smith, Langford's Basic Photography, 9th edition, Focal Press, 2010
